notes: Balance sheets for Apple, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Broadcom, Tesla, Oracle, AMD, Intel, CoreWeave, Palantir, Netflix and SpaceX come from stockanalysis.com's quarterly balance-sheet pages (newest column) because sec.gov refuses scripts and Apple's release PDF extracts out of order; NVIDIA's and Microsoft's come from their own releases. Dates differ by fiscal calendar: NVIDIA 26 Jul 2026, Broadcom 2 Aug 2026, Oracle 31 Aug 2026, CoreWeave 30 Jun 2026 (its Q3 report is not out), the rest 26-30 Sep 2026. On stockanalysis.com 'Total Debt' includes lease liabilities and 'PP&E' can include finance-lease assets (Apple's 63.7 versus 52.1 in Apple's own release). Equity is common equity as the page labels it. The brief's companiesmarketcap.com /pe-ratio/ pages do not exist; per-company /<slug>/pe-ratio/ pages were used. Its other per-company pages were stale for Apple (383.3 billion total assets versus 404.5 in Apple's release), so they were not used. Not found as fetchable text: Oracle's lease commitments not yet commenced, Meta's, Alphabet's and Amazon's purchase commitments, Microsoft's lease commitments (all in 10-Qs on sec.gov). NVIDIA's commitments are read from a secondary article quoting the 10-Q.
openQuestions: Are the stockanalysis.com balance sheets, a secondary aggregator, acceptable for the 13 non-release companies, or should a later pass replace them with 10-Q text?
Should lease commitments not yet commenced (Oracle, Microsoft, Meta) be added from 10-Q text, which needs a fetch route that sec.gov permits?
CoreWeave's Q3 2026 balance sheet is due after this date; refresh then.
